headline: South Africa's fortress: Korea's possession goes unrewarded
story: Korea Republic came to Monterrey seeking to impose control, and for long periods they did—61 per cent possession, 5.7 high-pressure phases, the ball at their feet for most of the afternoon. But South Africa, deployed in a disciplined 4-2-3-1, never panicked. They recovered the ball in 24.3 seconds on average, forced 40 turnovers to Korea's 28, and waited. That patience was rewarded in the 63rd minute when a swift counter-attack produced the game's only goal: low expected value (0.09 xG), maximum effect.

Korea's dominance was real, their 0.74 xG matching superior play: a missed chance at 7' (0.21 xG), saved efforts at 60' and 90+3' (0.17, 0.36). But they never broke through. South Africa's Thapelo Maseko (8.0 rating) orchestrated suffocating defence, with Mbokazi (7.8) and Mudau (7.7) imposing flank discipline. Korea's Kim Min-Jae, Han-beom Lee, and Young-woo Seol, all 6.9–7.0, found no space. The match was decided not by possession, but by transitions.

keyMoment.text: South Africa converts a 0.09 xG chance; clinical finishing overcomes Korea's possession dominance.

home.verdict: A masterclass in defensive discipline and transition football; they survived Korea's late siege.
points: Forced 40 turnovers to Korea's 28—the midfield battle won through intensity, not possession.
Recovery time of 24.3 seconds bought them the space to break; slow transitions would have buried them.
Maseko's 8.0 rating anchored the defence; one lapse at 90+3' nearly cost them a 0.36 xG concession.

away.verdict: Possession and pressure alone do not win matches; clinical finishing would have changed everything.
points: Three quality chances (0.21, 0.17, 0.36 xG) summing to 0.74 xG went begging—conversion was the missing link.
28 forced turnovers vs South Africa's 40 revealed a midfield out-battled in transition; Korea's 3-4-2-1 lacked cover.
5.7 high-press phases without reward suggest the press lacked coordination; Kim Min-Jae (7.0) could not turn dominance into clean sheets.

statLine: South Africa won with 30 per cent possession and a 0.09 xG goal, while Korea's 61 per cent control and 0.74 xG went unrewarded—a reminder that football is not played in possession metres.
